chapter_theme: Ainkurunuru 471 to 480, Peyanar's mullai decade of the bard (பாணன் பத்து): the waiting wife reproaches the bard who comes from her absent husband, doubts his promises and calls him loveless; the husband, still away on campaign, posts the bard with her and asks him again and again for her words; and in the last poem the bard renounces his lord for ignoring her tears.

471.reading: The heroine tells the bard that the valiant lord has surely abandoned her, so that her bangles slip, her body withers and her painted many-petalled eyes are clouded with floods of tears; the bard seems not to grasp it and keeps on coming, and she asks what sort of decency that is of theirs.
471.nuance: The reproach is double: the lord is called மறங்கெழு குருசில், great in valour, in the same breath as the man who deserted her, and the bard's very persistence in coming is turned into evidence against the party he serves. The plural அவர் lumps bard and master together.

thinai_evidence.note: she waits at home while the warrior stays away and his bard keeps coming

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; she speaks to the bard who keeps coming from the absent lord; the friend speaking for her is also possible

472.reading: The heroine tells the bard of the skilled small lute that the season his people fixed has come and stands here; even if they do not learn of it from her, what pains her is that they feel no shame for the false word on their own side.
472.nuance: She does not ask for his return; she grieves that the promise-breaker is not ashamed. The season standing (வந்துநின்றது) is itself the accusation, so she need not speak it.

thinai_evidence.note: the appointed season has arrived while she waits

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; she speaks to the bard when the promised season has come

comparisons.tenor: the bard, if he leaves her

473.reading: The heroine tells the skilled bard that if, thinking of his much-praised lord, he wants to go back to him, then he should not abandon her the way the liars did who brought her this bitter, hard longing.
473.nuance: The bard has been staying with her and now wants to rejoin his master; she fears he too will turn out one of the பொய்வலாளர், the men skilled in lies. Whether மறாவாதீமே means 'do not forget us' or 'do not refuse us' is not settled by the text.

thinai_evidence.note: she waits in longing and fears even the bard's going

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; she speaks to the bard who wants to return to his lord

474.reading: The friend tells the heroine that the bard says he will bring back the absent man, driving his tall chariot with swift horses so hard that the roads are cut, with his battle-strong army that wrecked the forts of his foes, so that her flawless bright forehead may shine again; fine indeed, she says, is the bard's sense.
474.nuance: நன்றால் அம்ம may be plain praise of the bard's comfort or dry irony at a promise he cannot keep; the decade's other poems, which doubt the bard, lean toward the second. The war matter of lines 2 and 3 tells us the man is away on a king's campaign, the usual mullai absence.

thinai_evidence.note: the bard promises to bring back the man for whom she waits

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; the friend reports the bard's promise to the heroine; the speaker is inferred from the third-person பாணனது and the bard's words to சுடர்நுதல்

475.reading: The heroine says that the bard of the small lute, seeing her shoulders withered so that they lost their firmness and her eyes robbed of their shapely beauty, grieved greatly; he is not like his master, who left her for all her ardent love; the bard has the greater love.
475.nuance: The servant is set against the master by the master's own woman: the bard's pity becomes the measure of the lord's want of it. The word read here as நொடிநிலை is obscure.

thinai_evidence.note: she wastes while the man who left stays away

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; she speaks of the bard in the third person, most likely to her friend

476.reading: Now that the massed clouds roar at the height of the rains and the green mullai creeper has flowered for its season, the heroine asks the loveless bard whether the land where his master went also has this loveless evening, when herdsmen with many cows put together their leaf garlands.
476.nuance: அன்பு இல் is used twice, once of the evening and once of the bard, so the hour and the messenger stand on the same side against her. The herdsmen coming in at dusk do what the absent man does not; they set the hour but are not tagged as iraicchi because the poem's question does not rest on their act.

thinai_evidence.note: the rainy season and the evening of the pasture land

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; she speaks to the bard at evening in the rains

477.reading: The man tells the bard that if he stays a little while as comforting company for the helpless heart of her whose cool flower-like long eyes are spreading with pallor, who labours in grief full of bitterness and hard longing, he will soon see the man's chariot.
477.nuance: Here the decade turns to the man's side: the bard's staying with the woman, which she resented in 471, is his master's instruction, and the chariot is promised as the bard's reward.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife waits and the man promises his chariot's return

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; the man, still away, sends the bard to stay with his wife

478.reading: The man asks the bard of the fine lute in the mullai mode to tell him what his beloved said, she who, saying he had stayed away too long, spread the word of his cruelty, her forehead withered, imagining something else, wasted by her great sickness.
478.nuance: He asks to hear the charge against himself: கொடுமை தூற்றி, she broadcast his cruelty. பிறிதுநினைந்து may mean she suspected another woman or simply feared the worst.

thinai_evidence.note: she has waited too long for the man away

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; the man, still away, asks the bard for his wife's words

479.reading: The man asks the excellent bard to tell him again, since it is sweet each time it is told, what the woman of cool flower-like eyes said, now that he is held off by the lands between and every day the merciless north wind, thick with heavy dew, mocks his loneliness.
479.nuance: The wind mocks his solitude, not hers: the man is shown suffering the season too. Asking for the report again and again makes the message a substitute for return.

thinai_evidence.note: the dewy season of waiting apart

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; the man asks the bard to repeat his wife's words; மாண is taken as an address to the bard

480.reading: The bard tells the man that they are no longer his bards and he is no longer their lord, since he is not shaken on hearing the cry of his beloved, who laments in her lonely house and sheds tears from her moist-lidded painted eyes.
480.nuance: The bond of patron and bard is formally dissolved over the man's treatment of his wife. It closes a decade that opened with the wife counting the bard among the man's party: in the end he sides with her.

thinai_evidence.note: the wife waits alone in the house

thurai_akam.speaker: paanan
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (பாணன் பத்து) puts the bard at the centre of the decade; the bard speaks to the absent man

links.note: 471's heroine resents that the bard keeps coming (இன்னும் வருதி); in 477 the man tells the bard to stay a little as her comfort (உயவுத்துணை).
links.teaches: Read together, the bard's persistence that the wife takes for indifference turns out to be the man's own order, so the decade shows one act judged from both ends of the separation.

links.note: In 475 the heroine says the bard grieves for her more than his master does; in 480 the bard himself renounces his master over her tears.
links.teaches: The sympathy the wife reads in the bard's face becomes, by the decade's last poem, a spoken break with the patron, so the decade moves the go-between from the man's party to the woman's.

links.note: Natrinai 86 blesses the men as அறவர் for coming back before the season they named; Ainkurunuru 472 says the season has come and its makers feel no shame at their false word.
links.teaches: The named season works as a vow with a moral verdict either way: kept early it earns the title of righteous men, broken it is charged as shamelessness, so the return date was judged as truthfulness rather than as mere timing.

links.note: Both wives put to the bard a question about the evening of the herding land in the rains (Akananuru: மாலையும் உள்ளார் ஆயின் ... பாண; Ainkurunuru: மாலையும் உடைத்தோ ... பாண).
links.teaches: Ainkurunuru gives only the wife's accusing question and her name for him, loveless bard, while Akananuru tells it from the bard's side, who could not answer, played and prayed and went toward the man, so the pair shows the question was one the bard had no words for.

links.note: Both have the waiting woman put a question to or about evening: the Kural asks evening whether its partner is as hard as hers; Ainkurunuru asks whether his land has this loveless evening at all.
links.teaches: The Kural explains the man's calm by a hard heart that evening shares, the Ainkurunuru by a land the evening may not reach, so the two give the waiting woman two answers to why he does not suffer the hour she suffers.

links.note: In 477 the man tells the bard to stay with his grieving wife (துனி மலி துயரமொடு) and promises his chariot; in Akananuru 314 the wife has asked the bard what will become of her, and the man arrives to end her துனிகொள் பருவரல்.
links.teaches: The man's instruction and promise in Ainkurunuru and the friend's welcome in Akananuru are two ends of one convention: the bard is posted with the wife to field her question, and the chariot's coming is what answers it.

links.note: In Akananuru 244 the bard's report of the wife's words makes the man yoke the horses at once, his work being done; in 479 the man, still kept away by the lands between, asks to hear her words again because they are sweet.
links.teaches: The same report of the wife's words could be a spur that ends the campaign or a comfort savoured while the man stays on, so the bard's message did different work depending on whether the man's task was finished.

links.note: In Purananuru 144 bards see a woman weeping over Pekan's neglect and rebuke him; in 475 the heroine says the bard wept over her wasting more than his master.
links.teaches: Puram shows the bard's pity for the neglected woman turned into a public rebuke of his patron, and akam shows the woman herself noticing that pity and setting it against her lord's coldness, so the bard's tears were a recognised charge against the man in both genres.

links.note: In Purananuru 145 Paranar asks as his only gift that Pekan ride to the grieving woman tonight; in 480 the bard, unheard, declares that he is no longer the man's bard.
links.teaches: Puram's bard spends his claim on the patron to win the woman's cause, while the Ainkurunuru bard, his plea having failed, gives up the claim itself, so the pair shows the patron bond as the bard's leverage and its renunciation as his last resort.

source_issues: The colophon gives no thurai for any poem of the decade; speakers are inferred from the poems and the decade title.
471 line 1: எவ்வளை is hard to divide (எம் வளை, 'my/our bangles', is assumed); line 4 போலாய் is read as 'you do not seem to'; the reading is marked uncertain.
473 line 5: மறாவாதீமே may stand for மறவாதீமே ('do not forget') or be a form of மறு ('refuse'); the reading is marked uncertain.
475 line 1: நொடிநிலை is an obscure word; its sense ('firm state') is a guess and the reading is marked uncertain.
